n: Jesus looks up to heaven and prays. This chapter, often called the Intercessory Prayer, is the longest recorded prayer of Jesus. He begins: the hour has come — glorify your Son so the Son can glorify you.

f.w: lifted up his eyes to heaven
the hour is come

n: The Father has given the Son authority over all humanity so that he can give eternal life to those the Father has given him.

f.w: power over all flesh

n: Jesus defines eternal life: to know the only true God and Jesus Christ whom he sent. It is not just endless existence but a personal, growing relationship with the Father and the Son.

f.w: this is life eternal, that they might know thee

n: Jesus reports to his Father that he has glorified him on earth and finished the work he was given — speaking with confidence even before the cross.

f.w: I have finished the work

n: He asks to be restored to the glory he shared with the Father before the world was created — a clear statement of his premortal existence.

f.w: the glory which I had with thee before the world was

n: He has revealed the Father’s name — his true nature — to the disciples given him out of the world. They belonged to the Father, he gave them to Jesus, and they have kept God’s word.

f.w: manifested thy name
f.g: In Hebrew thought, a “name” stands for a person’s character and identity.

n: They now understand that everything Jesus has comes from the Father.

f.w: are of thee

n: He gave them the Father’s words; they received them and know for sure that he came from the Father.

f.w: have known surely

n: Here he prays specifically for his disciples, who belong to the Father.

f.w: I pray not for the world
f.g: Not a rejection of the world (see verse 21), but focused intercession for these disciples now.

n: All that is his is the Father’s and all that is the Father’s is his, and he is glorified in his disciples.

f.w: all mine are thine, and thine are mine

n: As he leaves the world, he asks the Holy Father to protect the disciples, keeping them united as the Father and Son are one.

f.w: that they may be one, as we are
f.g: The unity of the disciples is modeled on that of the Father and the Son — unity of heart and purpose.

n: While with them, Jesus protected them and lost none except the “son of perdition,” Judas, who chose destruction as scripture foretold.

f.w: the son of perdition
f.g: perdition = ruin, destruction. Here an idiom for one headed to ruin.

n: Now he is coming to the Father, and he prays aloud so they may have his joy fully in themselves.

f.w: my joy fulfilled in themselves

n: He has given them God’s word, and the world hates them, because like him they don’t belong to the world.

f.w: the world hath hated them

n: He doesn’t ask the Father to remove them from the world, but to protect them from the evil one. Disciples are meant to live in the world without being ruled by it.

f.w: keep them from the evil

n: He repeats: they are not of the world, just as he is not.

f.w: They are not of the world

n: He asks the Father to make them holy through truth — God’s word is truth.

f.w: Sanctify them
f.g: sanctify = make holy, set apart for God’s purposes.

f.w: thy word is truth

n: Just as the Father sent him into the world, he sends them. The word “apostle” means “one who is sent.”

f.w: even so have I also sent them into the world

n: For their sake he consecrates himself — gives himself entirely as a sacrifice — so they can be made holy through the truth.

f.w: I sanctify myself
f.g: Jesus dedicates himself to the sacrifice he is about to offer.

n: He widens his prayer to include all who will later believe through the apostles’ testimony — including believers today.

f.w: them also which shall believe on me through their word

n: He prays that all believers may be one, just as the Father is in him and he in the Father, so the world will believe the Father sent him. Unity among disciples is itself a witness of Christ.

f.w: That they all may be one

n: He has given them the glory the Father gave him, so they can share that same unity.

f.w: the glory which thou gavest me I have given them

n: Christ in them and the Father in Christ, so they can be perfected in unity — and the world will know that the Father loves them as he loves his Son.

f.w: made perfect in one
hast loved them, as thou hast loved me

n: His deepest wish: that those given him may be with him where he is and see his glory, given in love before the world’s foundation.

f.w: be with me where I am
before the foundation of the world

n: Addressing his “righteous Father,” he notes that the world hasn’t known the Father, but he has, and his disciples know the Father sent him.

f.w: O righteous Father
f.g: Jesus addresses God as Father six times in this prayer.

n: He has made the Father known and will keep doing so, so that the Father’s love for the Son may be in them, and Christ himself in them.

f.w: the love wherewith thou hast loved me may be in them
